correctness.rationale: Any total-dominating set needs at least 2 vertices on each shore; any 2+2 works. On 6 vertices Dominator can obtain <=3 vertices and cannot win. For n>=4 four disjoint within-shore pairs, two per side, supply a force-one-from-each pairing strategy in either start convention and the gamma_t lower bound forces 4 moves. Every transversal of a four-pair certificate is a 2+2 selection, so a cross-pair would change the shore count under flipping its choice; thus precisely two within-shore pairs per part. Matching count is 3*C(n,4) independently per shore.
